what: lever attribution: what each remedy bought in paired discrimination on omissions, and what it did to the judge's operating point
lands_at: Section 7, 'Scope, format and voting move the point, not the curve'

columns.lever: the remedy, in the terms a practitioner chooses it in
columns.delta_display: paired delta with its basis; a span where the lever has four matched per-design comparisons
columns.operating_point: what the same change did to single-note detection and false alarms
columns.substrate: the pairs, clean twins and replicates the row is measured over

reading_rule.rule: strict win rates must never be quoted across designs that differ in sample count: a finer aggregate splits ties and inflates the count

gate.why: v3m-08 beats seed_fc_score on VALID by +7.3pp paired and +22.9pp det@FA<=10%; the gate needs >2pp on both

caption: **What each lever bought, and what it did to the judge's operating point.** Paired discrimination is the tie-adjusted probability that an errored note scores below its own verified-clean twin, so 0.500 is a coin flip and a lever worth +0.04 buys four correctly ordered pairs in every hundred, only where a clean twin exists to compare against. The first three levers are quoted as the span of four per-design deltas, each holding the other two choices fixed, because a single headline delta would hide how far the spans overlap: criterion and format are indistinguishable on the mean (+0.052 against +0.053) and ensembling is smallest (+0.036). The reading rule this table carries: strict win rates must never be quoted across designs that differ in sample count, because a finer aggregate splits ties and inflates the count. The completeness-scored pair is the case in point. Asking eight times rather than once takes the strict win rate on omissions from 27% to 43%, but over the same 293 pairs the tie rate falls from 63% to 41%, and once half the tie mass is counted the paired figure moves 0.585 to 0.634. That is a lever worth +0.049, not sixteen points. Every paired figure in this paper is tie-adjusted for that reason.

rows.lever: What the judge is told to check
rows.change: faithfulness only, to faithfulness and completeness
rows.delta_basis: four per-design deltas, holding format and sample count fixed
rows.operating_point: Detection rises in all four comparisons, from 1.0-9.6% before to 4.7-42.3% after, and false alarms rise with it, 1.5-8.9% to 5.7-32.1%; of the eight designs only the two yes/no completeness ones have detection that clears their own false alarms (z 2.71 and 3.25), and they do it at 31.8% and 32.1% false alarms.
rows.substrate: the eight designs, 495-pair evaluation set, 3 replicates (879 omission records, 336 clean records)

rows.change: a yes/no verdict, to a 0-to-10 score
rows.delta_basis: four per-design deltas, holding criterion and sample count fixed
rows.operating_point: Both rates fall together, detection from 9.6-42.3% to 1.0-8.3% and false alarms from 7.4-32.1% to 1.5-6.5%, so the scored designs are quieter rather than sharper: their detection never clears their own false alarms by more than 1.02 standard errors.
rows.substrate: the eight designs, 495-pair evaluation set, 3 replicates (879 omission records, 336 clean records)

rows.lever: How many times it is asked
rows.change: once, to eight times with the extremes trimmed
rows.delta_basis: four per-design deltas, holding criterion and format fixed
rows.operating_point: The operating point barely moves: the largest change is the completeness-scored pair, detection 4.7% to 8.3% at false alarms 5.7% to 6.5%, and no scored design's detection separates from its own false alarms at either sample count.
rows.substrate: the eight designs, 495-pair evaluation set, 3 replicates (879 omission records, 336 clean records)

rows.lever: How the prompt words the omission instruction
rows.change: the deployed faithfulness judge in three wordings, as shipped, with its omissions-are-not-errors exclusion deleted, and with an affirmative instruction to report omissions added
rows.delta_basis: the affirmative instruction against the same prompt with the exclusion merely deleted; paired 0.518 as shipped, 0.505 deleted, 0.556 affirmative
rows.operating_point: The affirmative instruction takes detection from 13.1% to 25.6% (77 and 150 of 586 omission judgements, against 16.4% as shipped) while false alarms hold at 27 of 224 clean judgements (12.1%) for all three wordings, the same rate though not the same notes; deleting the exclusion on its own takes paired discrimination from 0.518 to 0.505 and detection from 16.4% to 13.1%.
rows.substrate: three wordings of the deployed judge, 495-pair evaluation set, 2 replicates (586 omission records, 224 clean records)

rows.lever: Letting an optimiser rewrite the prompt
rows.change: reflective prompt evolution, aimed at the per-fact checker and at the best monolithic judge
rows.delta_display: +0.052 and +0.073 on the acceptance sets, -0.023 and +0.004 held out
rows.delta_basis: two search legs, each measured on the 20-consultation acceptance set that chose the winner and then once on the 47-consultation held-out set
rows.operating_point: Held out, the per-fact checker's winner gains 0.8 points of detection (22 against 21 of 131 omissions) at the same 8.5% false alarms, and the monolithic winner loses 4.6 points (11 against 17 of 131) at the same 6.4%. The earlier campaign's winner carried a false-alarm rate of 9.1% (2 of 22 clean development notes) to 21.9% (49 of 224) on data it had never seen, at 23.0% detection (135 of 586).
rows.substrate: acceptance set 48 omission pairs and 20 clean twins; held-out set 131 omission pairs and 47 clean twins, one replicate; the earlier campaign's winner on the 495-pair evaluation set, 2 replicates
